sources.label: LA Sanitation: S.A.F.E. Centers (household hazardous waste)
recycLA: What goes in your blue bin (City of LA guide)

bins.name: Blue bin
bins.accepts: Recycling: paper, cardboard, glass, metal, plastics 1, 2 & 5

bins.name: Green bin
bins.accepts: Organics: food scraps, food-soiled paper, yard trimmings

bins.name: Black bin
bins.accepts: Trash: what can't be recycled, composted or donated

bins.name: Special drop-off
bins.accepts: Not in any bin: batteries, e-waste, spray cans (S.A.F.E. Centers)

prep: Empty it and rinse it clean
plastic_bottle.why: The blue bin takes clean plastic bottles and jugs made from plastics 1, 2 and 5.

prep: Empty it and rinse it clean
plastic_container.why: Clean tubs like yogurt and margarine containers are accepted if they are plastic 1, 2 or 5.

prep: Cups labeled compostable go in the black bin too
plastic_cup.why: The blue bin lists only plastic bottles, jugs and tubs, so cups go in the black bin.

prep: Screw it back onto the empty bottle or tub
Loose, flimsy or unmarked lids: black bin
plastic_lid_cap.why: Bottle caps are made of plastic 2 or 5, which the blue bin takes, and LASAN says to keep caps on bottles.

prep: Never in the blue or green bin
plastic_bag_film.why: LA's blue bin does not take plastic bags or film plastic, and they are kept out of the green bin too.

snack_wrapper.why: Candy and snack wrappers are film plastic, which LA's recycling guide lists as trash.

foam.why: Styrofoam is not recyclable in LA and goes in the black bin.

prep: Untreated wood or bamboo utensils: green bin
plastic_utensil_straw.why: The blue bin lists only plastic bottles, jugs and tubs, so plastic utensils and straws go in the black bin.

prep: Greasy or food-soiled paper: green bin
paper.why: Junk mail, newspapers and other clean, dry paper are accepted.

prep: Greasy or food-soiled bags: green bin
paper_bag.why: Clean paper goes in the blue bin, and food-soiled paper goes in the green bin.

cardboard.why: Cereal boxes and flattened delivery boxes are accepted.

prep: Leftover crusts can go in with it
pizza_box.why: LASAN lists greasy pizza boxes as food-soiled paper for the green bin.

prep: Paper only, with no plastic or wax coating
soiled_paper.why: Food-soiled paper like napkins, paper towels and coffee filters goes in the green bin.

prep: Cups with no plastic or wax lining: green bin
paper_cup.why: LA's recycling guide lists disposable coffee cups as trash because most have a plastic lining.

prep: Empty it and rinse it clean
carton.why: LASAN lists cartons with the blue bin recyclables.

prep: Empty it and rinse it clean
metal_can.why: Aluminum and tin cans are accepted.

prep: Take it to a S.A.F.E. Center
Never in the blue or black bin
aerosol_can.why: LASAN lists aerosol cans as household hazardous waste for S.A.F.E. Centers.

prep: Appliances and large metal: book a free bulky item pickup
metal_lid_scrap.why: LA's blue bin list names aluminum and tin cans and clean foil, not lids or scrap metal, so small metal items go in the black bin.

prep: Empty it and rinse it clean
glass_bottle_jar.why: Glass bottles and jars of any color are accepted.

prep: Wrap sharp pieces so no one gets cut
drinking_glass_ceramic.why: Broken glass and dishware can't be recycled and go in the black bin.

prep: Collect it in a bowl or kitchen pail
Empty it loose into the green bin
food_scraps.why: Food scraps, including meat, bones and dairy, go in the green bin.

prep: Put it in loose, not in plastic bags
Too much? Use the free yearly brush pickup
yard_waste.why: Flowers, grass clippings, tree and bush trimmings and clean untreated wood go in the green bin.

prep: Take it to a S.A.F.E. Center
Small household batteries can go in a library battery bucket
battery.why: Batteries are household hazardous waste and can start fires, so they never go in a bin.

prep: Take out the batteries if you can
Drop it off at a S.A.F.E. Center
electronics.why: LASAN collects electronic waste at S.A.F.E. Centers, not in the curbside bins.

prep: Donate it if it is clean and wearable
Worn-out or torn fabric: black bin
textile.why: The black bin takes worn-out cloth that is unsuitable for donation, and textiles are not on the blue or green bin lists.

shoes.why: Shoes are not on the blue or green bin lists, so worn-out pairs go in the black bin with other non-reusable items.

cigarette_butt.why: Cigarette butts can't be recycled or composted, so they go in the black bin.

blister_pack.why: Blister packs mix plastic and foil and are not a bottle, jug or tub, so they go in the black bin.

rope_string.why: Cords, rope and other tanglers jam the sorting machines at the recycling plant.

prep: Empty it as far as you can
squeezable_tube.why: Tubes are not bottles, jugs or tubs, and those are the only plastics the blue bin takes.

mask_gloves.why: Disposable masks and gloves can't be recycled or composted, so they go in the black bin.
